title: QBR Blueprint: Standard + Enterprise Decks and Renewal Playbook
content:
Purpose: 1-pager for CS reps and AMs to build consistent QBR decks for standard (SMB/mid-market) customers and enterprise customers. Includes: slide-by-slide template, speaker notes, renewal risk tracker CSV, and a step-by-step playbook for pre-QBR prep and post-QBR follow-up.

Usage: Copy the appropriate slide group (STANDARD or ENTERPRISE) into the customer-facing deck. Use the Renewal Risk Tracker to prioritize outreach in the 90/60/30 days before renewal. Attach relevant Rollout/Adoption OKRs and recent telemetry exports (Console -> Token-level breakdown).

---
Slide order (master outline)
1. Cover slide
   - Title: Customer QBR — [Customer name] / [Quarter] / [AM name]
   - Speaker notes: Keep to 30–45 seconds. High-level success headline.

2. Executive summary (1 slide)
   - One-line business outcome tied to Redwood (cost reduction, latency improvement, feature adoption).
   - Top ask at the end (e.g., expansion request, exec sponsor meeting, renewal commitment).

3. Health snapshot (1 slide)
   - Standard: usage trend (tokens/month), error rate, latency p50/p95, embedding calls, top routes.
   - Enterprise: add per-route SLA observability, dedicated vs hosted usage breakdown, private deployments note.

4. Adoption & outcomes (2 slides)
   - Standard: feature adoption (chat, rerank, embeddings), sample success stories.
   - Enterprise: mapping to business units, cost-centralization, compliance milestones (SOC2/ISO), integration status with internal infra (VPC, KMS).

5. Performance & economics (2 slides)
   - Cost per 1k tokens trend, model variants used, batching/quantization recommendations applied.
   - Enterprise: reserve vs burst capacity utilization, estimated savings from Optimize suggestions, forecasted spend under current usage profile.

6. Risks & mitigation (1 slide)
   - Top 3 risks (latency spikes, model regressions, security/permissions), mitigation plan and owner.

7. Renewal & expansion (1 slide)
   - Renewal date, ARR, renewal likelihood, proposed upsell motions.

8. Roadmap & asks (1–2 slides)
   - Near-term product roadmap items relevant to customer, timing, and how we’ll measure impact.

9. Action plan and next steps (1 slide)
   - Clear owners and dates.

10. Appendix: Data dumps, network diagrams, POC configs (enterprise).

---
Standard vs Enterprise variations (quick checklist)
- Standard decks: concise, 8–10 slides max, focus on usage growth and product wins, AM + CSM present.
- Enterprise decks: 12–16 slides, include technical appendix, SLA adherence, security/compliance section, finance-facing cost model, and a dedicated renewal MOU slide. Include exec-level summary page for screening by customer execs.

Speaker notes: short bullets under each slide. Call out required visuals (time series charts, stacked bar by model, table of top 10 endpoints).

Renewal Risk Tracker (CSV rows for copy/paste)
customer,account_owner,renewal_date,term,ARR,renewal_risk_score,primary_concern,last_touch,next_action,action_owner,notes

Scoring rubric (use to compute renewal_risk_score)
- High: multiple concerns open, <60 days to renewal, adoption plateau, exec sponsor inactive.
- Medium: 60–90 days to renewal or single blocker.
- Low: >90 days, multiple adoption signals, engaged exec sponsor.

Pre-QBR playbook (30–14 days)
- 30d: Run QBR telemetry export (Console -> Exports) for last 6 months; build health snapshot. Create draft slides. Open internal ticket (JIRA- CS-<customer>) for any engineering asks.
- 21d: Meet with Customer Success Engineer (CSE) for technical appendix; validate latency/SLO charts.
- 14d: Share draft with AM/CSM and customer-facing champion for feedback. Add any contract/compliance artifacts for enterprise.

Final prep (14–1 days)
- 10d: Run renewal risk rubric. If high risk, schedule pre-QBR executive prep call.
- 5d: Send calendar invite to customer with agenda and expected attendees. 
- 2d: Final QA of slides; include back-up slides for deep-dive topics.
- 1d: Dry run with internal team. Confirm ask messaging (contract terms, expansion items).

Post-QBR playbook (0–30 days)
- Day 0–2: Send meeting recap with agreed actions and owners. Update Renewal Tracker.
- Day 3–14: If renewal in <60d, schedule commercial sync with sales. Attach proposed quote.
- Day 14–30: Execute agreed technical work items; confirm completion in Jira; close blockers.

Renewal play motions (examples)
- Low-effort expansion: propose model upgrades for top routes (+10% price).
- Mid-effort: propose Dedicated pool + committed throughput (reduce unit cost).
- Executive motion (enterprise): Align exec sponsor and propose 12–24 month custom SLA/license with platform fee.

Templates & snippets to include in the deck (copy/paste)
- Executive headline: "[Customer] reduced inference costs by X% vs baseline using Redwood Optimize and Dedicated pools."
- Ask slide snippet: "We recommend renewing at [term] with committed capacity of [GPUs] for predictable performance. Next step: sign MOU by [date]."
- Risk snippet: "Open items: 1) Latency regression on /chat route; 2) SOC2 evidence requested for Q3 audit. Owners: CSE + Security."

Example visuals to attach (filenames or dashboard refs)
- token-trend-last-180d.png
- p95-latency-by-route.png
- cost-per-1k-tokens-by-model.csv (attach)
- roadmap-impact-expected.csv

Operational notes and quick links
- Use Console -> Dashboards -> Customer -> Export to CSV for the charts referenced.
- Confluence QBR playbook (linked) contains prior decks and historical action logs.
- If private deploy or VPC discussion: pull Private Deployments runbook and security checklist (Confluence).

Open questions / TODOs (for internal doc)
- Add pre-built chart templates (Google Sheets) to auto-populate health slide.
- Create a one-click export from Console for cost forecast under different commit profiles.
- Draft commercial MOU template for enterprise renewals (legal review required).

Notes to self (choppy, keep)
- Keep standard deck <10 slides. Customer-facing language should avoid engineering jargon.
- For enterprise, bring finance and security SMEs into the QBR at least once per year.
- Link to example decks: see Confluence page and internal drive folder.

Action items (owners)
- Update shared chart templates: Devon Chen (due 2026-03-10)
- Draft MOU template: Priya Reddy + Legal (due 2026-04-01)

Version notes: v0.9 initial draft adapted from playbook workshop 2025-10-19. This doc is intentionally prescriptive but editable; flag any customer-specific deviations in the Renewal Tracker notes field.
